solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Singer absolutely rebuffed by textile designer

parts.note: William Morris, the Victorian designer of wallpapers and fabrics

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the word for absolutely is read backwards

parts.note: an emphatic 'absolutely!' means yes

explanation.surface: A vocalist is snubbed by a fabric designer.
explanation.walkthrough: William Morris was the Victorian designer of the Arts and Crafts movement; 'rebuffed' turns the affirmative round.
explanation.definitionFit: Steven Patrick Morrissey is the singer once fronting the Smiths.

clue.text: River missed by elderly sleuth in wood

indicators.note: the river is something the sleuth misses, so its letter goes from her name

parts.note: Miss Marple, Agatha Christie's elderly amateur detective

explanation.surface: An old detective overlooks a river while out in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Marple is Agatha Christie's elderly detective; 'missed by' drops her R.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple is a hardwood timber, from the tree of the same name.

clue.text: Prominent new family appearing in tabloid

indicators.note: the new family appear within the tabloid's word, so these letters go inside it

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a downmarket newspaper
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A newly famous family turns up in the gossip papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranking officer or member is one of senior, high-standing position.

clue.text: Noticing outrageously surprised cry's disguised

indicators.note: behaving outrageously suggests wild disorder, so the letters of noticing are scrambled

parts.note: O! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone spots a shocked shout coming from a person in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageously' signals the anagram; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Going incognito means concealing one's true identity, as with a disguise.

clue.text: Bard pronounced tribal leader's equal

indicators.note: pronounced says the phrase is spoken aloud and then spelt as the answer sounds

parts.note: a sheikh is an Arab tribal chief, and his peer is his equal: sheikh's peer

explanation.surface: A poet is said to rank alongside a tribal chief.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bard of Avon is the standing nickname for England's greatest playwright.

clue.text: Still legendary creature's not completely visible

indicators.note: not completely means the creature's name is cut short of its final letter

parts.note: the yeti is the abominable snowman of Himalayan legend

explanation.surface: A mythical beast remains only partly in view.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet and still are synonyms in the sense of 'nevertheless' or 'up to now'.

clue.text: Woman and chap in middle American town

indicators.note: in middle asks for the central letters of each of the two words, woman and chap

explanation.surface: A woman and a man sit at the heart of a US town.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters of wOMAn and cHAp give OMA and HA.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in Nebraska, in the American Midwest.

clue.text: Addicted to tune being broadcast

parts.note: to be on drugs is to be addicted to them
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: Someone hooked on a song hears it played on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that is live and transmitting is said to be on the air.

clue.text: Warm female appears in a moral tale

indicators.note: the female appears within the phrase, so her letter goes inside it

parts.note: a fable is a short story pointing a moral

explanation.surface: A kindly woman features in a story with a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a friendly, genial manner towards other people.

clue.text: Model sportsman losing right to work in pool

indicators.note: losing means the sportsman sheds the letter for right

parts.note: an archer is one who shoots arrows in competition
to type is the work done in a typing pool

explanation.surface: A sportsman drops out to labour in a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops one R from ARCHER to give ARCHE. A typing pool was an office of typists, so 'pool' is not water.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the original pattern or perfect example of which others are copies.

clue.text: Old man accepting an excellent remedy for disease

indicators.note: the father's word takes in the other letters, so they go inside it

parts.note: one's old man is one's father, pa
ace means first-rate

explanation.surface: Father welcomes a superb cure for illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed cure-all for every ailment.

clue.text: Disastrous bringing folios in for good trade

indicators.note: bringing introduces the folios as letters brought into the word
in for says the folios take the place of the letter for good

parts.note: tragic means calamitous
ff is the abbreviation for folios, as in page references

explanation.surface: A calamity forces a bookseller to deal in old pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic means commerce or dealing, especially illicit trade in goods.

clue.text: Dallas company for example snatching victory

indicators.note: the example abbreviation grabs the victory word and holds it inside

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A Texan firm grabs a win, as one might.
explanation.definitionFit: In the TV soap Dallas, the Ewing family ran the oil business Ewing Oil.

clue.text: Appalling manager somewhat disheartened crowd

parts.note: an exec is an executive, a manager

indicators.note: somewhat disheartened says part of the crowd word's centre is removed

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly mob

explanation.surface: A boss faces a crowd that has lost heart, and it is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat disheartened' takes away one of the two middle Bs of RABBLE, leaving RABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means abominably bad, deserving to be cursed.

clue.text: Cool teen rude about stage school

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about the stage word, holding it inside
rude in the sense of crude or rough-made, so the letters of cool teen are reworked

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or contest

explanation.surface: A cool teenager is rude about drama school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude' turns COOL TEEN into ETONCOLE, which goes 'about' LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English private boarding school near Windsor.

clue.text: Fuddy-duddy endlessly causing confusion

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a fogy is an old-fashioned, fussy person

explanation.surface: An old stick-in-the-mud keeps muddling things.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a fog means being bewildered or mentally clouded.

clue.text: Backing provided by Pliny, patrician Rome arranged dodgy dealings

indicators.note: backing means the word for provided is turned around

parts.note: provided means if, as in 'provided that'

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the three words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A Roman writer and a noble set up a shady scheme together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns IF into FI; 'arranged' shuffles PLINY PATRICIAN ROME into the remaining eighteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial impropriety is misconduct with money, such as fraud or misuse of funds.

clue.text: See 14 down
Unusually good ground yields element

parts.note: rare can mean exceptionally fine, as in a rare talent
earth is soil or ground

explanation.surface: Exceptionally fertile soil produces a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare earths are the lanthanide metals, each one a chemical element.

clue.text: Church probes Cranmer on mutilated magician

indicators.note: the church letters probe into the scrambled letters, going inside them
mutilated means disfigured, so the letters of Cranmer on are rearranged

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The Church investigates the disfigured Archbishop Cranmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Cranmer was the Tudor Archbishop of Canterbury burnt at the stake; 'mutilated' turns CRANMER ON into NECROMANR, and CE goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A necromancer is a sorcerer who claims to raise the dead, a kind of wizard.

clue.text: There's prison work in ancient coastal town

parts.note: the can is slang for jail
an opus is a work, especially a musical composition

explanation.surface: Inmates labour in an old seaside settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Canopus was an ancient Egyptian port near modern Alexandria.

clue.text: Detective in study

definitions.meaning: a private ... is a private investigator

explanation.surface: A sleuth works in the study.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: slang for a private investigator, and the verb meaning to look over carefully.

clue.text: Coleridge upset having lost identity as artist

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the poet's letters are thrown into a new order
having lost says the letters of identity are missing from the shuffled poet

parts.note: ID is short for identity, as in an ID card

explanation.surface: The poet Coleridge is distressed at losing his sense of self.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I and D from COLERIDGE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Cretan-born painter of Renaissance Spain.

clue.text: Matchless — nothing keeps cricket side level with English

indicators.note: the word for nothing keeps the other letters inside it

parts.note: nil means zero
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
par means on a level, as in on a par

explanation.surface: A blank scoreline holds a cricket team level with England.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil means having no equal, unrivalled.

clue.text: When position brings advantage

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
to set something is to place or position it

explanation.surface: Getting into the right spot gives one an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or resource, a benefit to its holder.

clue.text: Reportedly an island crew

indicators.note: reportedly says the island's word is heard aloud and spelt as another

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river, especially the Thames

explanation.surface: Supposedly a team of rowers lives on an isle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing eight is a boat crew of eight oarsmen.

clue.text: Square it with American for holy work

parts.note: a T-square, so T stands for square

explanation.surface: Settle up with a Yank for a religious book.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus is the New Testament epistle written to a companion of St Paul.

clue.text: Current doctor protects by putting thick coat on

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the doctor's letters protect the other word by enclosing it

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
past means by, as in going by or past a place

explanation.surface: A doctor in a current keeps safe by wearing a heavy coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the painting technique of laying pigment on thickly.

clue.text: Sort of a yahoo

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange, so the letters of of a are put in order

explanation.surface: A kind of lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo, after Swift's brutes in Gulliver's Travels, is a coarse, stupid person.

clue.text: Firm guarantee

definitions.meaning: firm here means serious and resolute
a pledge or deposit given as a token of a bargain

explanation.surface: A company's promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: sincere and determined, and a token payment securing a deal, as in earnest money.

clue.text: Barman is the last an officer embraces

indicators.note: the officer embraces the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: Lt is a lieutenant
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A bartender says he is the final one an officer hugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' is not a bartender but a man of musical bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt, the Hungarian composer and pianist, wrote music measured in bars.

clue.text: Husband stops following topless dancing in strip clubs

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: the husband stops up the scrambled letters, sitting inside them
dancing means the letters of topless jig about into a new order

explanation.surface: A husband stops going to watch topless dancing in seedy clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' turns TOPLESS into LESPOTS; H goes into it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleshpots are places of sensual or sexual entertainment, such as sleazy nightclubs.
